# H<sub>8</sub>: SSR(8,8) dissociation

For simple hydrogen chains, in which two to eight hydrogen atoms are pulled apart simultaneously, our method's dissociation curves closely track near-exact reference calculations across all chain lengths tested.

BH\&HLYP/6-31G(d) · 1934SI-6SA-REKS(8,8) · R 0.70–4.925 Å · 171 points · FCI 43

[Curves](#curves) · [Numbers](#numbers) · [Calculations](#calculations)

## Curves

H₈ SSR(8,8): S0 energy along R(H–H) from 0.7 to 4.925 Å with FCI in the same basis; natural occupations below

H₈ SSR(8,8): S0 energy along R(H–H) from 0.7 to 4.925 Å with FCI in the same basis; natural occupations below

PECs for H<sub>8</sub> from SSR(8,8)/BH\&HLYP compared with FCI (circles); KS-DFT (dashed grey); thin curves denote excited states, and the short dashed segment marks the energy of isolated atoms. H<sub>8</sub> uses 6-31G\*, a smaller basis set required because FCI becomes computationally intractable for larger ones. Triangles denote single-point FCI references computed with a larger basis set: cc-pVDZ. Since FCI with a small basis set cannot fully capture the correlation energy, the FCI curve lies somewhat above the corresponding SSR curve. DFT-based methods are less sensitive to basis set size than FCI \[[Goerigk and Grimme 2011](https://reksstudio.github.io/v2/manual/reference/index.md#goerigk2011-benchmark)] \[[Bursch et al. 2022](https://reksstudio.github.io/v2/manual/reference/index.md#bursch2022-protocols)], so the depth of the SSR minimum at the equilibrium geometry agrees better with the FCI single-point values obtained at the larger basis set. Lower panel: natural occupations n<sub>i</sub> of S0; dotted: R<sub>e</sub> of S0.

H8: active orbitals along the dissociation

Active SA-REKS orbitals φ(z) on the chain axis along the bond coordinate (z in units of R); bars: n of S0 of the natural orbital each orbital dominates.

## Calculations

The REKS/SSR calculations for the hydrogen chains were executed using a state-averaged ensemble that included the PPS1 configuration and all OSSx configurations generated within the same GVB orbital pairing scheme. To ensure stable SCF convergence, a high-spin determinant was incorporated into the ensembles. All density functional calculations utilized the BH\&HLYP functional. For the REKS/SSR calculations, initial guess orbitals were generated via standard KS-DFT calculations using the identical density functional and basis set. Potential energy curves were scanned at increments of 0.01–0.025 Å. Additionally, reference full configuration interaction calculations were carried out using the Psi4 package.

Method: SI-SA-REKS(8,8) = SSR(8,8); 1934SI-6SA-REKS(8,8)

SA pool: PPS1 0.166667, OSS1 0.166667, OSS2 0.166667, OSS3 0.166667, OSS4 0.166667, all-α determinant 0.166667

SI: catalogue configuration set full; 2S = 0: 1934 configurations

Functional, basis: BH\&HLYP/6-31G(d)

SCF: DF, energy/density thresholds 1.00e-07/1.00e-05, grid 75 × 302

Orbital solver: TRAH

Coordinate: R(H–H); linear H chain, equal spacing R(H–H)

R window: R 0.700–4.925 Å, 171 points
